newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls on dlr/mark arbitrage, rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls on dlr/mark arbitrage, rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,682-1,688 per dollar, down from the opening's 1,678-1,682 on the local market due to active dollar/mark arbitrage and a pending cut in the main lev interest rate, dealers said.

* Dealers said the dollar rise on international markets on Thursday prompted dollar/mark arbitrage by local banks in line with a recent trend of building up mark positions ahead of the lev peg to the mark as anchor in a currency board.

* The mark share in the local forex market daily turnover has steadily increased from one to 10 percent in May to 17-19 percent in the past two days as more local banks converted dollars into the anchor currency, traders said.
* The lev will be pegged at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 to the mark under a currency board system, to be launched on July 1.
* The lev closed at 975-978 per mark, a touch firmer from the morning's 975-980 in line with the mark fall against the dollar on international markets.

* Foreign currency demand rose further in the afternoon after the Bulgarian National Bank informed local banks that it will cut its main interest rate to 35.76 percent annually from 47.28 percent now, to take effect from Monday, dealers said.

* There was a large amount of free levs in the banking system following rejection of most bids at the daily auctions of Finance ministry's four-week discount T-bills this week. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
